name: National Gallery of Arts Tirana
known: Shqiptarja (15 October 2025) calls Adela Demetja the new director and the first woman in the post.
Wikipedia's infobox lists Erzen Shkololli as director.
Acting director Entela Çipa put it at 1 billion lek in January 2023 and called it a government investment (Shqiptarja, from her Report TV interview).

name: Tirana Art Lab
known: The website lists Adela Demetja as former founding director, 2010 to 2025, and Resina Meçani as executive director (Tirana Art Lab website).

What it runs: residencies, exhibitions, workshops, performances, lectures, publications, and from 2023 "Curating with Care", an alternative curatorial education programme with the Istituto Italiano di Cultura in Tirana.

name: Musée National des Beaux-Arts d'Alger
known: Directors have included Jean Alazard (1930 to 1960), Jean de Maisonseul (1962 to 1975) and Malika Dorbani Bouabdellah (until 1994) (French Wikipedia).

name: Musée Public National d'Art Moderne et Contemporain (MAMA)
known: Curators: Mohamed Djehiche (2007 to 2016), Nadira Aklouche Laggoune (2016 to 2020) and Kamel Righi (2020 to August 2023) (French Wikipedia).

name: Agostinho Neto Memorial (Memorial Dr. António Agostinho Neto)
known: It is under the President of the Republic, supervised through the Minister of State and head of the Casa Civil (art. 5).
The director sends annual accounts to the supervising body and the Tribunal de Contas (art. 10).

A public establishment under the President of the Republic, supervised through the head of the Casa Civil (Presidential Decree 302/21); it holds Neto's sarcophagus, a museum, a library and an exhibition gallery, and works with the Fundação Dr.
Its statute, Presidential Decree 302/21, lists its revenue sources, puts its budget inside the State Budget and has the director submit annual accounts to the Tribunal de Contas.
President of the Republic, through the Minister of State and Head of the Civil House

name: Fundação Sindika Dokolo
known: Dokolo, a Congolese collector, began the collection in 2004 with the Angolan artist and curator Fernando Alvim and set up the foundation in 2006 (The Art Newspaper, 2017).
Named for its founder, the husband of Isabel dos Santos, daughter of former president José Eduardo dos Santos.
Founders' fortune tied to Angolan state oil and diamond deals.

name: Nesr Art Foundation
known: The Art Newspaper describes the founders as members of the Lebanese-Belgian family behind the Webcor Group, and Wissam Nesr as Webcor's chief executive.
The Art Newspaper in 2021 named Paula Nascimento as chair of the artistic committee.
The founders' business: Webcor Group, described as "one of Angola's major food manufacturing entities", led by Wissam Nesr (Food Business Africa, 10 June 2022).
In May 2026 Proparco and BIC-BRED (Suisse) SA announced trade finance for Webcor, with Sergio Limonti named as its CEO (Proparco).
Opened in 2021 with a residency for Angolan and Lusophone African artists; the artistic committee is chaired by Paula Nascimento.

name: Colección de Arte Amalia Lacroze de Fortabat
known: Founded by María Amalia Lacroze de Fortabat (1921 to 2012), longtime chairperson and chief stockholder of the cement maker Loma Negra, who set aside part of her own art collection for it.
Named for its founder.
The artistic director is Germán Barraza (museum website).
A 2014 prosecutors' office report said Loma Negra, which the founder controlled, gained from the 1976 coup.

name: Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes
known: Created by decree of President José Evaristo Uriburu in 1895 with Eduardo Schiaffino as first director.
Andrés Duprat has been executive director since December 2015, appointed after a public competition (Spanish Wikipedia).
The museum's site shows undated sponsor logos and names its director and two coordinators.

name: Museo de Arte Latinoamericano de Buenos Aires (MALBA)
known: Founded by businessman Eduardo Costantini, who donated 223 works from his personal collection in 2001, the base of the museum.
Founder donations: 2,191,394,826 pesos, 11.5 percent; other donations: 1,676,948,861 pesos, 8.8 percent.

Perfil (Adriana Lorusso, 12 November 2020) reported that Costantini would keep paying for most of Malba's activities through a dedicated fund for the next 15 years and would keep the veto power the original statute gives him as founder.

name: Museo de Arte Moderno de Buenos Aires
known: Created in 1956 by decree 3527/56 on the initiative of Rafael Squirru, its first director.

name: Palacio Libertad
known: The centre's site carries programme, agenda and news pages, with a director named in a news post.

name: Museo Casa sobre el Arroyo (Casa del Puente)
